findings.source_quote:
What joy the happy earth to greet
    In new, bright raiment clad!
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace the translation of these two lines with a faithful rendering that preserves the sense "What joy to greet the happy earth, clothed in new, bright raiment!" e.g.: "Hvilken fryd å møte den glade jord,
    Kledd i ny, lys drakt!" — keep the HTML structure unchanged.

    I nytt, lyst draktelag!

Use a more idiomatic and accurate Norwegian rendering of "I greet Thy going forth;" e.g.: "Jeg hilser Din utgang" or "Jeg hilser Din utferd" — replace only the text inside the

Restore the intended meaning that these are "new births" that are "more divine." Suggested translation: "Disse nyfødte, mer guddommelige fødsler:" or, more idiomatically, "Disse nyfødte og mer guddommelige fødsler:" — keep punctuation and tags unchanged.

findings.source_quote: This new-born glow of faith so strong,
findings.suggested_fix:
The phrase "glow of faith" was rendered as "mot til tro" (courage to faith), which changes the meaning. Suggestion: "Denne nyfødte troens glød så sterk," or "Denne nyfødte, så sterke troens glød," — replace only the clause inside the

tag.
findings.translation_quote: Dette nyfødte mot til tro så sterk,

findings.suggested_fix:
The compound noun "draktelag" is non‑idiomatic in Bokmål. Use "drakt" or "drakt!" or "kledd i ny, lys drakt!" to be idiomatic. Replace only the phrase inside the

tag.

The alt text is acceptable but could be slightly more natural as "Hvite orkideer med lilla midt" or "Hvite orkideer med lilla midtparti" if you prefer; this is optional. No HTML structural change required.
